preCheck.prompt: You walk the same route every day and stop noticing the pallet stack by the door. What is this called?

options.text: Normalization of risk — the familiar stops registering as risky
options.why: Exactly: repeated exposure without incident makes the risky feel normal.
A risk assessment is a structured process; quietly stopping noticing is the opposite.
Perception is noticing — this is the failure to notice.

preCheck.prompt: Which is the better reason to report a near-miss where nobody was hurt?

options.text: It reveals a weakness in the system while it is still free to fix
options.why: Yes — a near-miss is information about a hole nobody has paid for yet.
Blame suppresses reporting and usually misses the system causes.

options.text: Because paperwork requires it after any event
options.why: Compliance-only reporting misses the point — the learning.
Right — how probable, times how bad.
Neither measures risk.
Cost shapes which control you choose, not the risk itself.

preCheck.prompt: A cable crosses a walkway inside a proper yellow cable ramp. Is this a hazard to report?

options.text: No — the ramp is the control; it is a controlled condition
options.why: Correct. Learning to tell controlled conditions from hazards keeps reporting credible.

options.text: Yes — all cables on floors are hazards
options.why: Not when properly ramped and outside the walkway.
By then it is an incident, not a report.

preCheck.prompt: In the hierarchy of controls, which is generally MOST effective?

options.why: Yes (NIOSH). PPE is the last line, not the first.
PPE is the least effective tier — it protects one person from consequences, not causes.
Training is an administrative control — valuable, but below elimination/substitution/engineering.

postCheck.prompt: A new stack appears by the fire exit on Monday. By Friday nobody sees it. The most useful next step is…

options.text: A marked staging area with a hard rule that exits stay clear (fix the system that made blocking easy)
options.why: Yes — change the condition so the unsafe state is not the convenient state.

options.text: Remind people on Friday that exits must stay clear
options.why: A reminder repeats weekly what the layout causes daily.
Cameras record; they do not keep the exit clear.

postCheck.prompt: Your risk rating should change most when…

options.text: Severity rises — e.g. the same trip hazard is now at the top of a mezzanine stair
options.why: Severity dominates when it becomes life-changing.
Complaints are data, not the rating itself.
Cost informs the control choice, not the risk.

postCheck.prompt: The replay's root causes included 'no owner or schedule for mirror checks'. This is a…

options.text: System cause — a control decayed because nobody maintained it
options.why: Yes — systems let controls fail quietly.
The behavior was trusting a lying mirror; the decay behind it is a system cause.
The mirror's angle is a condition; the missing ownership is the system beneath it.

postCheck.prompt: Which report is most likely to get fast action from a busy supervisor?

options.text: Situation, hazard, impact, ask — with a specific location and request
options.why: Structured, complete, actable in seconds.

options.text: A long story that ends with 'so yeah, maybe someone should look'
options.why: No structure, no ask, no action.

options.text: A message to a group chat after your days off
options.why: Delayed and diffuse — nothing to act on.

postCheck.prompt: In the transfer zone, a loaded truck is parked straddling the pedestrian walkway with a load the driver cannot see over. The strongest first control is…

options.text: Keep the staging lane physically clear of the walkway (layout change)
options.why: Yes — engineering the conflict out beats managing it.
PPE tier — last, not first.

options.text: Ask drivers to be careful there
options.why: An instruction against a built-in conflict will lose.

transferReflection.prompt: Name one condition in your own workplace that 'looks risky but is controlled', and one that 'looks normal but is not'. What makes each what it is?
transferReflection.why: Transfer task: the discrimination skill applied outside the simulation.
